what_its_for: Brolucizumab is used to treat wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME). These are eye conditions where abnormal blood vessels grow in the back of your eye and leak fluid, which can blur your vision or cause vision loss. This medicine helps block the growth of those abnormal blood vessels and reduce the leaking, which can protect and sometimes improve your vision.
how_to_take: This medicine is NOT a pill or liquid you swallow. It is given as an injection directly into your eye by a trained eye doctor (ophthalmologist) in a clinic or doctor's office. Your eye will be numbed with anesthetic drops before the injection so you feel little to no pain. The procedure is quick, usually taking only a few minutes. Never try to inject this medicine yourself at home.
dosing: For wet AMD, you will usually receive one injection every month for the first 3 months (3 loading doses), and then your doctor will decide if you need injections every 8 or 12 weeks based on how your eye responds. For diabetic macular edema (DME), you will receive one injection every month for the first 6 months, then your doctor will reassess how often you need treatment. Always follow your doctor's schedule closely, as every patient's plan may be slightly different.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an injection appointment, contact your eye doctor's office as soon as possible to set up a new appointment. Do not skip treatments without talking to your doctor, because missing doses could allow the disease to get worse and cause more vision loss. Try to keep all scheduled appointments even if your vision seems to be improving.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled only by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. You do not need to store it at home. If for any reason you are given the medicine to bring to your appointment, keep it refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) in its original packaging to protect it from light. Do not freeze it. Keep it out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: After your injection, avoid rubbing or touching your treated eye, as this can increase the risk of infection. Avoid swimming, hot tubs, or getting water in your eye for at least 2 days after the injection unless your doctor says otherwise. Do not wear contact lenses on the day of the injection. Avoid driving immediately after your appointment if your vision is temporarily blurry — bring someone with you to drive you home. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your eye doctor RIGHT AWAY or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden vision loss or worsening vision, eye pain or increased eye discomfort after the injection, redness of the eye that gets worse, sensitivity to light, seeing floaters or flashes of light, or if the white part of your eye looks very red. These could be signs of a serious eye infection (endophthalmitis), retinal detachment, or dangerous inflammation inside the eye called retinal vasculitis or occlusion, which need immediate treatment. Also call your doctor if you have chest pain, trouble speaking, or weakness on one side of your body, as this medicine may rarely cause stroke or other serious blood clot events.
when_it_works: You may not notice vision improvement right away. Some patients begin to notice changes within the first few weeks to months of treatment, but results vary from person to person. The main goal of this medicine is to prevent further vision loss — improvement in vision is possible but not guaranteed for everyone. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular eye exams and imaging tests to check how well the treatment is working.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): This medicine is commonly used in older adults and no special dose adjustment is needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if this medicine can harm an unborn baby or pass into breast milk. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one month after the last injection. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is needed for kidney or liver issues, but always tell your doctor about any other health conditions you have. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old.
